name: @cloudsforge/wallet
description: The user-facing money API. Wallet registry, external wallet links and verification, deposit address assignment, withdrawal requests, conversions, transfers and the portfolio read. Owns no balances and no keys.

scripts._test: --test-concurrency=1 is required, not a preference: every database test file truncates this service's tables between cases, and node:test runs FILES in parallel by default. A TRUNCATE takes an AccessExclusiveLock, so one file's reset deadlocks against another file's inserts (40P01). Cases within a file already run in order.

_localDependencies: The @cloudsforge/* packages are consumed from sibling checkouts because none of them is
published yet. Once AD-02 lands they all become registry versions and these paths — plus the
two build contexts in the Dockerfile and the extra checkouts in CI — are deleted. Nothing else
Every sibling takes 'link:', not 'file:'. A 'file:' path PACKS the dependency, and each of
these packages declares files: ['dist'] with a publishConfig that points main/types at dist/.
Packing therefore installs a package whose exports resolve to a dist/ that has not been built,
while its 'main' in the working tree still says src/index.ts — the web template hit exactly
this and the symptom is an unresolvable import of a package that is plainly present. 'link:'
symlinks the checkout in place, so the working-tree manifest is the one that is read and the
package keeps using its own already-installed node_modules. That last part is also what
@cloudsforge/contracts-money needs: it depends on contracts-chain with the 'workspace:^'
protocol, which only resolves inside the contracts workspace.
@cloudsforge/contracts-chain is EXACT-PINNED on publish ('1.0.0'), never caret-ranged. wallet,
settlement, custody and indexer must agree byte-for-byte on confirmation depths and amount
maths; a skew there is not a 500, it is money credited at the wrong depth.
tsx is a runtime dependency for the same reason: the unpublished packages resolve to their
TypeScript sources. On publish their publishConfig points at dist/, tsx moves to
devDependencies, and the image runs 'node dist/index.js'.
